steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Can't wait any longer?

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: If what Kal'tsit said was true, then none of us can really afford to wait around.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Even while we walk this land, we are still a part of the sea. Those corrupted descendants are... in the process of changing the 'environment.'

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: In time, none of us will be spared. All we're doing now is sitting around waiting for the end to come.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: We're not the only ones sitting around though, and everyone's reasons are different.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Think about it more broadly. Who knows, maybe these lands aren't suited for our survival?

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs in agreement)

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Not harmonious enough.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: There's something I wanna try.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: Time to mix it up, all for the tunes!

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs in agreement)

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: So what exactly do you have in mind?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Uh... Well, we're not exactly accomplishing much over here.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Just treat it as a little pre-concert workout. Don't swim too far out, Frost.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: A workout. Huh. What about the rest of you?

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I think I'll pass.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Too lazy.

steps.name: Dan
steps.text: I can feel the inspiration on its way. It's so close. Just a liiittle bit more.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: ...Alright. (Riffs enthusiastically)

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: I'll be off then.

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: No, what did that woman and the Inquisitor do? How could they so easily erase the gift of the sea?!

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: Ægir... It must've been the Ægir. What the Ægir left behind, those strange machines! They must be destroyed!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Makes a slithering sound as it clings to the cultist's calves)

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: That's right, my brother, the Penal Battalion has this place surrounded, and we've failed to break through... We've nowhere to run.

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: But... our exalted prophet has returned to the sea.

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: All that's left... is to pave the way for Her.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Impatient slithering sounds)

steps.name: Out-of-Breath Cultist
steps.text: If they seek to hold back the tide, then let them dash against the rocks. My life is but one brick in a lengthy road.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Don't panic, it's just me. Why haven't you taken refuge yet?

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: M-Mayor Thiago... I was drunk and out as cold as a gloompincer, so I didn't hear anything.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: By the time I woke up, everything had gone to shit, and these disgusting things were all over the place.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: What happened here? Has the Inquisition sent anyone yet? What's going to happen to us?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: ...The great ocean is not guilty of any crime, but the Inquisition does not agree. They control the so-called law, and have condemned us as sinners.

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Soon enough, the Sea Terrors will return to the ocean. But I cannot allow the Inquisitors to condemn Gran Faro to death just like that.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: What are you talking about? Have you gone mad?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Mad? I'm not the one who's mad! I simply need to know! What can we do before the Inquisition destroys this town and rounds us all up to stand trial?!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: An Inquisitor has already arrived. I saw that clearly when hiding in a little alley. I've never seen one that old before, and they gave me the chills...

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: What are you gonna do then, Thiago? Go up to them and try to reason with them?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: We'll have to choose sides again, right?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: When the Ægir were taken away, most people looked on, just like that. They had a chance to stand up for them, but nobody stepped forward.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: Thiago, you—

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Now, we have another chance. Either watch the Inquisition put everyone in Gran Faro on trial, or—

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: Have you lost your marbles?! Inquisitor! Hey, Inquisitor! He can handle us all without raising a hand!

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Take me to them.

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: ...What are you talking about?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Drop the act. How long do you think I've lived in this town?

steps.name: Terrified Townsperson
steps.text: Alright, follow me. If your goal really is to take revenge on the Inquisitors...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Just what are you up to, Mayor Thiago?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Almost there.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This is already taking too long.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: S-Sorry.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It's not your fault. It's mine, for not having enough patience.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um... Doña Inquisitor, if you're worried about the others, you can go help them. I think I can handle things up here.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The High Inquisitor gave me a order to protect you. As you've seen, those monsters are everywhere. I can't just leave you alone.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But I don't want to be what's holding you back from joining the battle... I just—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: As long as you can light up this tower, then the High Inquisitor will have made the correct decision. I simply defer to his judgment.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Did your knowledge of the Eye of Iberia come from your parents?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yes. Or more precisely, it's the sum of all of Gran Faro's past. They gathered all the best lighthouse engineers in all of Iberia, or at least that's what my uncle told me.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The territory used to be demarcated by the Inquisition, until it was abandoned after a string of incidents involving the Ægir and the Church of the Deep.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I'm not trying to reopen old wounds, but I've been thinking. Before I left, I read the dossier about the sentence handed down at the time. ...No, never mind.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Do you hate the Inquisition?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um... To be honest...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: If there's anything that always hangs over the heads of the people back home, other than the ubiquitous dark clouds, it would be the word 'Inquisition.'

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: The town once glimmered, giving us the confidence to rebuild our homes. The workers and engineers gave everything they had to fight the disaster, but the Inquisition took everything before it even struck.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And do you still believe that today?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's the place I grew up in. Everything I've ever seen or heard has only reinforced that lesson.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: And, um, I'm sorry, ma'am.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You are simply stating your lived experiences, citizen. It is your actions that will prove your loyalty to Iberia.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Still, I'm astonished you had the guts to say all that in front of an Inquisitor.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I never would've dared, not until I came here... But, then I saw the Eye. For the longest time, it's only appeared in my dreams, nothing more than a sculpture sitting in the plaza.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Everyone in Gran Faro who came before me has passed this all down. Our duty, what we must do...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: It's all surging through me right now—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: —Um, ma'am, do you see something glimmering at the base of the lighthouse? Something blue, and sparkling like stars...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That's—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —The nethersea brand!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Do you really think you can fight me, Mister Knight?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You only care about the lighthouse. Why? Why do you cling to it so?

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Monstrous waves... Swallowing the sky...

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Even the stalk of wheat... consumed by silence. All things great and small... returned to nothing.

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Agitated slithering sounds)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: He can speak, but not command his kin. The Sea Terrors are in disarray.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Let us put an end to this.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Rasping roar) —!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: —What a surprise, Mister Knight. You're not moving like you were before.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Those are human movements. A charging wind-up, unique to Kuranta knights. What exactly are you?
The knight continues to ignore his two opponents. His attention is solely on the third.
Even with his attack, the towering lighthouse does not even shake. If even the Profound Silence failed to destroy the Eye, what chance does a lone knight have?
It bewilders him. It pushes him to try even harder.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Rasping murmur) Clouds, rolling hills, pillars of ash... arrayed across a hotbed of decay.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: The tides... unending...

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Violent slithering)

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You're injured, and the Sea Terrors are drawn to you.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: So it appears. Got a little scratched up on accident—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ngh...

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Step aside. You're no longer fit to fight.
Dario's eyes quickly dart across the Abyssal Hunter in front of him. Her movements had paused unnaturally a few times during the previous clash.
He's heard reports about her. She was involved in the Sal Viento experiments, but the woman who stands before him is completely different from the one who emerged from that fierce battle.
Who was she? And who is she now?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: They've hardly touched you, yet you seem barely able to stand.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Maybe an illness you contracted in Sal Viento?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...The scent of the sea is rather intoxicating, that's all.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Knight ...Comrade. Why, why must you gag on the air, and endure the heat? You'll never taste... the fruits of civilization.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Urgh...!
The ground is shaking.
Energy long-lost floods through the pipelines and into the broken body of the Eye of Iberia, prying open its eyelids.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: It has awakened. The entire island whispers the groans of its first light. Slowly it shakes off its winter, as if waking from centuries of hibernation.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...The cycle of all existence...

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Does not belong to the sea...
The knight lifts his head, gazing up from the shadow beneath the great lighthouse.
He is perplexed.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: That... is not the monstrous waves.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Where... are they?
Without drawing a single breath, as naturally as a shadow slants in the direction of the light, Specter brings down her weapon.
But the humanoid Seaborn in front of her avoids it, with logic-defying explosive force.
In midair, the knight looks far out into the distance.
He is listening, listening for the coming of new waves. And he will break them.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: ...Ishar... mla...

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Rasping growl) —Roci—nante—!

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Braying) —!!

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Unintelligible sounds) Chase!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Turns out, Mister Knight is afraid of the light.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Don't pursue him. He's not the only Seaborn like that out there. Our only duty is to defend this lighthouse.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: He's only lost interest in the lighthouse.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: I don't care about the motivations of monsters.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Are you saying... I'm also a monster?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: You are undergoing a transformation. I don't know whether this is something that happens with every Abyssal Hunter.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: But if necessary, this reef will be the last bit of land you'll ever step on.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You would still call this land, when we're clearly surrounded by ocean?

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Disasters change coastlines, not national boundaries.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: Every last centimeter of land swallowed by the Profound Silence is still subject to the laws of Iberia.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Laws, a virtuous word. Yet not all creatures recognize this virtue.

steps.name: High Inquisitor Dario
steps.text: ...Ready your blade.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: J-Just a little bit more!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithering sounds)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hurry up then! If this drags out any longer, the lighthouse will be swallowed up by the nethersea brand!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Ran into a little bit of a hitch!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: One of the auxiliary structures might've been damaged, b-but that would take too much time to investigate!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Just booting up the core facility will suffice. We still have to retrieve the flagship's coordinates, ideally reestablishing a connection with the line running along the coast—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I know, but— Those things might be even higher up!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Then keep going! Hurry!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I have to stay here... Turning on the lighthouse is as simple as pulling the most conspicuous lever, but I need to stay here and oversee the power system rebooting.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You should go, ma'am.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What? But if you're attacked by a Sea Terror that slipped through the net, we'll all—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I know! But I, I don't want to come up one step short, not now!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Those monsters— They only lashed out against humans because we invaded their nest, right?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: If that's the case, they won't keep destroying the facilities. If anything, getting into a fight will only make things more dangerous, so you should keep climbing instead!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...A conspicuous lever, right?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yeah, it should be obvious. Flip that, and at least the main facilities, including the lighting equipment, will start up again. ...Assuming what the log said is correct.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I'll be right back, Jordi.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The console... Well, this is it.
Nothing on the outside is visible from within the tower.
Could the Stultifera really not have sunk? How are they supposed to find that great dreadnought?
Is it too late for the Penal Battalion to come to their aid? Are the cultists of Gran Faro hiding even more secrets?
Just by pulling down on lever in her hand, all of these questions would be answered.
Irene should have been conflicted. She had accepted too much, learned much of the sea, and seen it all with her own eyes.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —Now's the time.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I hope you're ready, Irene.
Dazzling light penetrates the ocean, piercing through everything.
The light will lead the way. The light can dispel the darkness.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It worked!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hey, Jordi! Did you see that? We did it—

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithering sounds, rubbing against the wall)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Merda...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I didn't think you still had it in you to appreciate this sculpture.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Eye of Iberia... The offspring of the marriage between Ægir and Iberian technology. On land, each nomadic city can only seamlessly communicate within its own walls. Between cities, however, is like crossing a moat.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No system of communication can resolve the interference caused by Originium-rich zones. The only solution is to set up base stations that are at constant risk of being destroyed by Catastrophes.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I hear some countries have already adopted the technology of mobile base stations that navigate on a fixed route between cities. Their engineers are no different from those who guard our lighthouses.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Even today, humans still stumble about across this great land, blindly grasping for clues. We must still grope our way across Terra in near total darkness.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But, what of the ocean?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is no Originium in the ocean. The Ægir's communication technology vastly surpasses anything we have on land. The Eye of Iberia is not just a set of lighthouses.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: It is, of course, Iberia's vision. Very few people know that it was left to us by Breogan, as a microphone to connect all of Iberia.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: It's been a while, sir.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Your work was invaluable in allowing the Inquisition to respond so quickly to Dame Kal'tsit's proposal.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: How about you? Have you enjoyed your time in Gran Faro?

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: Compared to the other cities where our colleagues lay dormant, this place can hardly be considered dangerous.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: So, what have you found here?

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: My sincere apologies, sir. I doubt I know much more than you and the Dame.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: The order given to me by the High Inquisitor was to monitor Gran Faro for more potential enemies, those who would violate our laws and desecrate our country.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: My conclusion being, no. Not for the time being.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: When the Church's cultists appeared, you didn't notify your team in time.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: Correct, I determined those cultists to be impotent, and took advantage of the Penal Battalion's withdrawal as a prime opportunity to go after their true mastermind.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: And did you find them? Are there more... false bishops, presiding over the sea's invasion of the land?

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: Without concrete evidence, I can only speculate as to who their leader is.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: But Mayor Thiago, a worker from the Iberian hinterlands, is nominally the mayor of this town.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: Since the Eye of Iberia project was scrapped and the Inquisition made quick work of the traitors in Gran Faro, it's been no secret that he has been a pointed critic of the Inquisition.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Thiago... One of Gran Faro's laborers, sheltering the cultists. It would seem we have our next target, Dame Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: There's one other thing. Umm, Lord Carmen, the Penal Battalion seems to have come under attack.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: They've invested a Tercio just to quash the evil writhing in Gran Faro, to the point that it's a rare luxury to see even a single badge. What could they up against?

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: The nethersea brand has seeped through the ground to the surface, drawing a circle roughly fifty kilometers around Gran Faro.

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: And, it's a perfect circle, almost as if it was drawn with a compass...

steps.name: Calm Townsperson
steps.text: It's not the town that's been surrounded, though. It's us.
